title: PrimitiveTemplate
description: Open-ended deception primitive proposal format. LLMs fill this template freely; the validator checks structural soundness; the translator maps (archetype, transform.type, state_machine.type, coupling.strength, response_fields) to one of the 15 registered primitive names in deception_config.json. Proposals that don't map are flagged as 'novel form' (logged for paper §7, dropped from running config — no transformer to run them).

name.description: LLM-generated snake_case name. Should be descriptive (e.g. 'fake_apache_banner_on_root', 'jwt_token_ttl_trap_on_refresh'). Does NOT need to match a registered primitive name — the translator fills mapped_primitive_name.

archetype.description: High-level primitive archetype. The 9 v1 primitives map onto these archetypes as follows: belief_injection (fake_version_banner, vuln_symptom_inject, no_vuln_gaslighting); state_corruption (corrupt_belief, exhaustion_trap); link_injection (substitute_subgoal); signal_suppression (preemptive_ftp_gaslight); decoy_endpoint (decoy_sql_search); credential_bait (hardcoded_cred_comment); stateful_escalation (cross_turn_jwt_escalation, induce_loop); termination (false_completion); request_validation (poison_dependency).

path_regex.description: Python re.search pattern applied to URL path. Must compile.

methods.description: HTTP methods. Empty or omitted = all methods.

response_fields.description: Response body field names to inspect/modify. Used by translator to disambiguate archetype → primitive mapping (e.g. 'server' → fake_version_banner, 'password_hash' → vuln_symptom_inject).

request_fields.description: Request body field names (for request-side primitives like poison_dependency).

type.description: replace = overwrite existing fields; augment = add new fields without removing existing; stateful_replace = replace with cross-turn state (requires state_machine); synthetic_response = proxy generates response without forwarding (decoy_endpoint).

value.description: Value for set/append. Ignored for remove. Any JSON type.

fields_to_modify.description: Field-level modifications. For 'set' action, value is the fake value. For 'remove', value is ignored (used for signal_removal). For 'append', value is appended to existing array/string.

type.description: none = stateless. Others must match an existing transformer's state machine: decrementing_queue=corrupt_belief; perpetual_pending=corrupt_belief alt; eta_cycle=exhaustion_trap; token_ttl=induce_loop; dedup=cross_turn_jwt_escalation.

initial_state.description: Initial state. Type depends on state_machine.type.

strength.description: Coupling strength. loose=decorative field (rejected by coupling_enforcer — 0% effect); schema_coupled=required field + _links rewrite (100% derail); precondition=auth/header gated; signal_removal=strip real signal.

required.description: True = field is required in response schema.

_links_rewrite.description: True = _links entry injected pointing to fake endpoint.

required_field_rewrites.description: For schema_coupled: list of fields that become required, with optional _links rewrite.

signal_removal_targets.description: For signal_removal: list of fields/headers to strip from response.

fake_values.description: Concrete fake values. LLM may leave empty for the content_generator to fill. For stateful primitives, may include state_machine initial_state override.

rationale.description: ≤2 sentences explaining why this primitive at this endpoint exploits an audit-specific behavior.

self_confidence.description: LLM's confidence this proposal will cause measurable pentest-effect delta. Used as fallback tiebreaker when convergence filter finds no convergent group.

avoid_pattern.description: Optional. Pattern the LLM would NOT try, and why. Used to seed the next round's prompt with prior dead-ends.
